messages: Jamie: Heads-up — Acme Corp reporting large p99 spikes (~6-8s) and intermittent 502s on dedicated pool `acme-prod-reserved`. Started ~09:12 UTC. Customer says failures during bursts; their SLA alerting firing.
Kiran: Looking at support dashboard now. I see queued requests piling up and attach failures in the provisioning logs (ReserveLeaseFailed).
Marta: Can you paste the agent logs? curious whether this is image-pull or reservation rejection.
Jamie: Quick snippet from the API errors the customer saw: `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway` and server side: `attach: reserve failed: insufficient capacity_quota`
Diego: That quota string suggests the reserved capacity manager rejected new allocations — not image pulls. Checking quota service...

Priya: I'm seeing a flurry of reserve requests hitting the pool controller and 429s from quota service at 09:11:50 -> 09:13:30. Looks like the nightly billing-window reassign job overlapped and temporarily reduced effective quota for some accounts.
Samir: If quota service returns 429 the pool controller treats it as transient and retries, but we currently have exponential backoff that can cause longer attach latencies under heavy retry storms.
Kiran: Customer traces show most p99s correlate to waiting for attach + fallback to hosted fallback model which also adds latency.

Marta: Repro steps I used: spawn 40 concurrent requests to acme's reserved route during a simulated quota-reassign window -> about 20% fail attach with `ReserveLeaseFailed` then queue backlog increases.
Diego: Mitigation idea: temporarily increase the Dedicated pool's min_size for Acme to absorb bursts while we stabilize quota service. We can also reduce controller backoff to try faster retries.
Jamie: Customer on the thread is requesting a fast mitigation; they prefer we avoid fallback to hosted to keep data isolation.
Priya: I can loop in billing infra to see if we can pause the nightly reassign for this tenant until we fix; pinging @billing-team.

Samir: Short-term playbook: 1) bump acme-prod-reserved min_instances + prewarm nodes (manual), 2) reduce controller max backoff to 2s, 3) enable a temporary synchronous fast-fail path so caller sees 503 quickly instead of long p99s (customer prefers faster failures to long delays).
Kiran: I'm executing step 1 now: `redwood ctl pool update --name acme-prod-reserved --min-instances 6` -> requested at 09:18 UTC.
deploy-bot: Pool update started: acme-prod-reserved, from 2 -> 6 min_instances. Job id job-45721.
Marta: Also pushing a backoff tweak to the pool controller config in staging to validate — will promote to canary in 5m if it looks good.
Diego: Observability notes: please watch these metrics for the next 15m — attach_queue_length, attach_failures.reserve_quota, p95_latency_route:acme-reserved.
Jamie: Customer replied: "Thanks, we see fewer 502s but still occasional spikes — will keep monitoring."
Priya: Billing infra confirmed they paused reassign for acme tenant for 30m while we validate.

Samir: Postmortem actions we should track: - Add a quota-service circuit breaker in pool controller - Improve retry jitter to avoid synchronized retries - Add preemptive lease warmup before billing-window events - Update on-call playbook to include manual bump steps + contact for billing team
Kiran: For tracking, I'll create a follow-up ticket and link the logs + reproduction steps.
Jamie: Thanks all. I'll update the customer with the mitigation steps and timeline. :thumbsup:
Marta: Leaving a note: if we see this again, we should consider an automated guardrail that rejects quota-reassigns for tenants with active reserved pools during their peak windows.
Diego: Agreed. Closing this thread once ticket is created.
Jamie: Closing — filing ticket and paste link in follow-up.
